A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenARM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference-alignment experiments, inference timings, weak-to-strong guidance, multi-objective evaluations, and an appendix reward-coefficient sensitivity study.

after.justification: v2 retains original alignment experiments and additionally reports CARDS comparisons and measured training costs for autoregressive and trajectory-level reward models.

M1.justification: The autoregressive reward parameterization, preference-training objective, next-token sampling rule, and multi-objective combination remain unchanged in Equations (4)–(8). The added DPO and advantage-function discussion explains the existing method rather than changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HH-RLHF, UltraFeedback, AlpacaEval 2, and PKU-SafeRLHF-10K for the same general preference, weak-to-strong, and multi-objective tasks. The new training-cost comparison reuses HH-RLHF without introducing a distinct domain or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds CARDS to the HH-RLHF comparisons: Table 1 evaluates CARDS against DPO and GenARM against CARDS, and Table 2 includes CARDS inference time. Comparator membership in the other retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.1 introduces a controlled training-cost comparison using identical LLaMA-7B-SFT initialization, filtered HH-RLHF, and one epoch of LoRA training with alpha 16 and rank 8. The retained main evaluations keep their stated sample counts, metrics, and generation limits; newly disclosed quantization does not establish a setting change.

E4.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix B.2's reward-coefficient sensitivity study and Figure 9, which showed improvement followed by degradation as guidance increased. It adds Appendix C.1's analysis of training-time and parameter overhead. Existing token-reward and multi-objective qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes from point estimates to values with ± quantities throughout. Neither the table nor surrounding documentation defines these quantities or specifies run counts or seeds, so the change establishes new uncertainty reporting but not an identifiable increase in experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 1 updates retained values, including GenARM versus DPO's win-plus-half-tie score from 52.00 to 51.44±0.35, and adds GenARM versus CARDS at 57.27±0.19. Table 2 adds CARDS at 87.09 seconds. Appendix C.1 adds training times of 12,162 versus 11,722 seconds. Section 6.2 corrects the recovered performance gap from over 80% to over 70%; Figure 4 itself is unchanged. Figure 9's sensitivity results are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a conditional theoretical characterization linking an optimizer of Equation (5), under a regret preference model, to an optimal maximum-entropy RL advantage function. This cites existing theory without adding a proof. The original reward-equivalence definitions, expressiveness and uniqueness results, corollary, and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: autoregressive reward guidance, reward-class expressiveness, competitive alignment and efficiency, weak-to-strong guidance, and configurable multi-objective alignment. Additional comparisons support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 adds explanations of independence from DPO's reference policy and how token rewards can account for future returns. Appendix C.1 interprets measured overhead as small and compatible with fair comparisons. Conversely, removing the sensitivity discussion also removes its substantive warning about reward overoptimization and reliance on the base model for coherent output.

D1.justification: v2 documents LoRA settings, training times, and parameter counts for the new cost comparison. Appendix C.3 newly identifies checkpoint sources and GPTQ quantization for both 70B Tulu2 models; this is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed implementation. v1's explicit weak-to-strong inference setting beta=1 is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds a token-level reward related-work paragraph, CARDS, and references supporting the regret/advantage interpretation, including Knox and Hejna. The Gao reward-overoptimization citation disappears with the sensitivity discussion. Existing multi-objective and weak-to-strong related work moves to Appendix A rather than being removed.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. Changes include moving two related-work discussions into Appendix A, reorganizing mathematical and experimental appendices, adding explanatory subsections and cross-references, and localized wording and author/header edits. There is no extensive rewriting of the main argument.

P2.justification: The paper is reformatted throughout from the wider preprint layout to the narrower ICLR format, changing the title/author block, typography, margins, and figure placement. Figure 6 is substantially reduced and wrapped beside text, Figure 9 is removed, and Tables 1–2 expand for uncertainty entries and CARDS. Retained figure artwork is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The CARDS comparisons strengthen evidence for the central effectiveness and efficiency claims, while the training-cost comparison and checkpoint disclosures address useful documentation gaps. The corrected performance-gap statement also improves accuracy. These gains are partly offset by removing the coefficient-sensitivity evidence, its overoptimization qualification, and the weak-to-strong inference coefficient; the new ± quantities also remain undefined. The net improvement is limited.
